Title: Command Injection in fmt::say via std::system
Analysis:
Conceptual Payload: `\"; touch /tmp/pwned; #` as an argument to `fmt::say`.

Explanation:
The `fmt::say` function is designed for OS X to execute the `say` command-line utility via `std::system`. However, it constructs the command by simply formatting the arguments directly inside a shell-interpreted string using double quotes: `format("say \"{}\"", format(format_str, args...))`. There is a complete absence of any sanitization, escaping, or validation of the input arguments.

If any format argument contains a double quote followed by shell command metacharacters (e.g., `;`, `&&`, `|`), it breaks out of the `say` command's string argument and executes arbitrary commands under the system shell (e.g., `/bin/sh`). For example, passing `"; command; #` will result in the execution of `say ""; command; #"`, leading to arbitrary command execution.
